nodes.summary: For a rational subspace $V$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$, this is a fixed choice of a $\mathbb{Z}$-basis of the lattice $V \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$, indexed by $\{0, \dots, \dim V - 1\}$ and viewed as an $\mathbb{R}$-basis of $V$.
nodes.title: Chosen basis of a rational subspace

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a subspace of $\mathbb{R}^d$ and let $k$ be a natural number. For subspaces $v$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ write $\operatorname{dist}(v, x)$ for the distance between the subspaces $v$ and $x$, and for a rational subspace $v$ write $H(v)$ for its height. The diophantine exponent $\beta_k(x)$ of $x$ for approximation by $k$-dimensional rational subspaces is the infimum, taken in $[0, \infty]$, of the set of real…
nodes.title: Diophantine exponent

nodes.summary: For a line $x$ through the origin in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and a subspace $y$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$, the distance $\operatorname{dist}(x, y)$ is the infimum, over all lines $y'$ contained in $y$, of the distance $\operatorname{dist}(x, y')$ between the lines $x$ and $y'$. When $y = 0$ there is no such line and the value is $0$.
nodes.title: Distance from a line to a subspace

nodes.summary: For lines $x$ and $y$ through the origin in $\mathbb{R}^d$, the distance $\operatorname{dist}(x, y)$ is $\sin \theta$, where $\theta \in [0, \pi]$ is the angle between nonzero vectors spanning $x$ and $y$. This is the usual distance on the projective space.
nodes.title: Distance between lines

nodes.summary: For subspaces $x$ and $y$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$, the distance $\operatorname{dist}(x, y)$ is defined as follows. If $\dim y \le \dim x$, it is the supremum, over all lines $y'$ contained in $y$, of the distance $\operatorname{dist}(y', x)$ from the line $y'$ to the subspace $x$. nodes.title: Distance between subspaces

nodes.summary: For a rational subspace $V$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ of dimension $k$, let $v_1, \dots, v_k$ be the chosen basis of the lattice $V \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$. nodes.title: Height of a rational subspace

nodes.summary: For a subspace $V$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$, this is the set $V \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of integer points of $V$, as a $\mathbb{Z}$-submodule of $V$.
nodes.title: Integer points of a subspace

nodes.summary: $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is the $\mathbb{Z}$-submodule of $\mathbb{R}^d$ spanned by the standard basis vectors, that is, the lattice of points with integer coordinates.
nodes.title: The integer lattice

nodes.summary: A subspace $V$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ is rational if $V \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ is a full-rank lattice in $V$, that is, a discrete subgroup of $V$ that spans $V$ over $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Rational subspace

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
